newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Foreigners buy 612 bln won Korean stocks in net.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners buy 612 bln won Korean stocks in net.

text.p: Foreign investors bought a net 611.6 billion won worth of South Korean stocks on Friday, the first day of the increased foreign stock ownership limit, provisional figures from the Securities Supervisory Board showed.
The foreign share limit rose to 23 percent from 20 percent.
A securities watchdog statement said foreign investors bought 20.07 million shares valued at 668.6 billion won. They sold 3.81 million shares worth 57 billion won.
Foreign investors heavily bought primary blue chips, for which they have had to pay high premiums in over-the-counter trading.
Buying orders poured in for SK Telecom, POSCO, Samsung Electronics and Kookmin Bank, brokers said.
The statement said Kookmin Bank topped the foreign investors' buying list with 4.18 million shares, followed by Samsung Electronics with 2.76 million and POSCO with 2.66 million.
KEPCO shares led foreign selling, with 460,000 shares liquidated, the statement said. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647
